topics.title: Fog of war
topics.short: You see tiles, not always who stands on them. An enemy is seen only when your detection beats their stealth at that distance.
topics.long:
In the field you see the map your survivors have explored, but enemies only when someone actually spots them.

## Seeing someone

A hostile in sight range with a clear line is **seen** when your unit's detection, minus their stealth, minus 2.5 per tile past the first, is 0 or more. Next to you, always. See [[stealth]].

## Contacts

What you hear shows as a fuzzy marker, up to a tile off, for two rounds: gunfire within earshot, unseen enemies moving within 3 tiles, where an attack came from, a motion sensor going off.

## Lighting things up

- A **flare** lights a small area for a few rounds, for every side.
- A **motion sensor** warns you when something moves near it.
- A **scanner** sees hostiles nearby through walls and stealth.
- Firing reveals the shooter for a round or two.

## Night and weather

At night people see only 60% as far; fog, rain and dust cut sight further (see [[weather]]).

## Tips

- Use **Lookout** before moving into the unknown (see [[overwatch]]).

topics.title: Stealth and detection
topics.short: Stealth comes from Agility, light loads and quiet gear; detection from Perception and optics. Night adds +15 stealth against people and Husks.
topics.long:
## Stealth

Starts at 10, then:

- +0.3 per Agility point above 50 (less below).
- −1 per kg carried: loot is loud.
- Gear: rag coat +3, scout jacket +4, camo cloak +15; riot armor −10.
- Hurt legs or peg legs are loud.
- Perks such as Light Step and Ghost.

## Detection

Starts at 30, +0.5 per Perception point above 50, plus gear (binoculars +10, scanner +15), lookout and overwatch bonuses, all scaled by the head's condition.

## Light and weather

- Dawn and dusk +5 stealth, night +15, but not against the Linked's sensors, cameras or turrets.
- Rain, fog and dust add a little more.

## Range

Each tile of distance past the first takes 2.5 off detection. See [[fog]] for the full rule.

## Tips

- A heavy pack is the quickest way to get seen: drop or stash loot before sneaking.

topics.title: Ambush
topics.short: An attack from someone the target's side cannot see gets +20% to hit, ignores dodge and does ×1.25 damage. Bracing or an ally beside you blunts it.
topics.long:
When the target's side cannot see the attacker as the shot lands, it is an **ambush**.

## The bonus

- +20% hit chance.
- The target's dodge does not count.
- ×1.25 damage.

## Blunting it

- A **braced** target gives no ambush bonus at all (see [[overwatch]]).
- An ally next to the target, "watching each other's backs", halves it.

## Afterwards

The attacker is revealed to those it shot at for a round or two (guns longer than melee), they get a marker for where the attack came from, and anyone in earshot hears it. Enemies on overwatch may react.

## Both ways

The Linked plan ambushes: they lurk on overwatch and fire from the fog. Husks do not plan them but can stumble out of the dark.

## Tips

- Strike first from the dark, and keep your people in pairs.
- The hit-chance preview includes the ambush bonus (see [[hit_chance]]).

topics.title: Hit chance
topics.short: The attack's accuracy, minus dodge, cover, bracing and range, plus ambush, drone marks and radios. Always between 5% and 95%.
topics.long:
Hover an attack to see its hit chance. The breakdown below shows every term for the attack being previewed.

## The terms

- **Accuracy**: the weapon's, raised by skill and Perception, mods and perks; lowered by a hurt arm.
- **Dodge**: the target's (ignored in an ambush).
- **Cover**: the tile beside the target on your side: rubble 10%, a car 25%, cover 30%, a wall 40%, an armored vehicle 45%.
- **Brace**: +15% cover for a braced target.
- **Range**: −3% per tile past the first.
- **Ambush**: +20% if they cannot see you (see [[ambush]]).
- **Drone mark**: +10% (see [[drones]]).
- **Radio**: a bonus when two radios link your side.
- **Weather**: dust spoils ranged shots.
- **Bane**: some weapons are better against certain enemies, such as an EMP coil against the Linked.
- A ranged shot after moving this turn loses some accuracy.

The result is clamped between 5% and 95%.

## Tips

- Flank: shooting from where the target has no cover often beats moving closer.

topics.title: Overwatch, brace and lookout
topics.short: Overwatch (O) shoots what moves into view; Brace (B) adds cover and denies ambushes; Lookout (L) sees further and keeps your turn going.
topics.long:
Each costs 1 AP and lasts until the unit's next turn.

## Overwatch (O)

- Ends the turn. The AP you have left become **reactions**, at most 2.
- A free shot, at −10% accuracy, at each hostile that moves into or reveals itself within sight and reach.
- +10 detection while on watch. Reactions never set off other reactions, and allies are never shot.

## Brace (B)

- Ends the turn.
- +15% cover, and no ambush bonus against this unit.
- 1 AP less next turn.

## Lookout (L)

- Does **not** end the turn.
- +2 sight and +15 detection, more with Perception.

## Tips

- Lookout first, then move: you see what is waiting before you step into it.
- Brace a survivor you cannot get out of the open.
- The Linked use overwatch too: an enemy that stops moving may be waiting for you.

topics.title: Hacking
topics.short: Hack terminals, cameras, turrets, doors, lockers and relays with a kit or cyberdeck (H). Success opens them; failure raises the alarm.
topics.long:
Press **H** next to a device with a hacking kit (adjacent) or a cyberdeck (3 tiles, with line of sight). A hack costs 2 AP, less with perks.

## The chance

55% base, +0.5% per Hacking point, +0.4% per Intellect point above 50, plus the tool and perks, minus the device's difficulty. A device on the Linked Network is 15% harder unless a jammer covers it. Between 5% and 95%.

Some devices take more than one action of progress before the roll.

## On success

- **Terminal**: its items, the whole map explored, and a contact on every hidden enemy.
- **Camera**: it sees for you. **Turret**: it fires for you.
- **Door**: your side passes, others are locked out. **Locker**: its loot.
- **Relay**: jams the Network nearby and stops reinforcements.

## On failure

Noise (the alarm), Linked on the Network hunt the hacker, a shock to the arm, progress lost and a lockout of a few rounds.

## Tips

- Terminals are the best place to find schematics (see [[schematics]]).
- With the Override perk you can turn a Linked enemy for a couple of rounds.

topics.title: Scout drones
topics.short: Deploy a drone (K) to see over walls, fly it with the operator's AP, and with perks mark targets for +10% to hit. On the world map it scouts zones.
topics.long:
## In the field

- **Deploy** (K) on a free tile next to the operator; **Recall** (K) to pick it up.
- **Fly** (J) with the operator's AP, over any terrain, within control range (the drone's own, plus Drone Piloting).
- Its sight is your side's sight, so allies share it.
- The battery drops 1 a round, faster inside a jammer's field. Flat, or with its operator down, it lands and is left behind.
- Melee cannot reach it and Husks ignore it, but the Linked focus it.
- **Mark** (M, Spotter perk): a target seen through walls and stealth, +10% to hit for 2 rounds.
- **Payload** (P, Payload perk): drop a flare or motion sensor.
- Thunderstorms and dust storms ground it.

Medic, cargo and combat drones from the Electronics Lab add their own actions.

## On the world map

Send a drone to a rumored zone within its battery's reach. It reports back after a while: the zone is scouted and its neighbours rumored. Over dangerous zones it may be shot down, less likely with a skilled pilot. It needs a day to recharge after.

topics.title: Loot and carrying
topics.short: Caches, lockers and fallen enemies leave piles. Take one item or everything (F). Weight past 60% of capacity slows you.
topics.long:
## Where loot is

- **Caches** and **lockers** around the zone; lockers can be hacked open (see [[hacking]]).
- **Remains**: a killed enemy drops a pile from its own table, sometimes with a schematic.
- **Salvage** nodes you work for materials (see [[salvage]]).

## Taking it

- Pick up one item for 1 AP, or **Take all** (F) for the same, lightest items first, as much as fits.
- Drop an item for free.
- Perks such as Scavenger find more in caches.

## Weight

Carry capacity is 10 kg plus 0.3 kg per Strength point. Past 60% of it you move one tile less; past 85%, two less. Weight also costs stealth.

## Stashing

On an exit tile, stash an item (1 AP): it waits there for your next run in that zone. Next to your parked vehicle, load it into the cargo instead.

## Tips

- Better zones, night runs and some weather mean better loot, and more danger.

topics.title: Salvage
topics.short: Work rubble, dead trees, furniture, wrecked cars and dead electronics (I) for materials. It takes AP, makes noise and trains a skill.
topics.long:
Salvage nodes are scattered around each zone: rubble, dead trees, broken furniture, old bedding, wrecked cars, building shells and dead electronics.

## Working a node

- Stand next to it and press **I**. Most nodes cost 2 AP a go (bedding 1).
- Each go adds 1 work, more with the right tool: pickaxe or crowbar for rubble, a hand saw or machete for wood, a hacking kit for electronics.
- When enough work is in, one lot comes off: into your pack while it fits, the rest onto a pile.
- Each node holds a few lots.

## Skill

Each node uses a skill (Mining, Woodcutting, Tailoring, Crafting or Electronics). More skill means more yield, and the work trains it.

## Noise

Salvaging is loud. Idle enemies within earshot come looking, and other parties hear it.

## Wrecked cars

Cars also give vehicle parts: wheels, spare parts, fuel cans. Big parts like engines and chassis need your own vehicle parked nearby; a winch adds a roll (see [[vehicles]]).

topics.title: Extraction
topics.short: Leave the map (X) from an exit tile or next to your vehicle, with whatever you carry. Anyone left behind does not come home.
topics.long:
Press **X** on an exit tile, or on any tile next to your parked vehicle, to take a survivor out.

## Who goes

- The survivor and everything they carry.
- A downed ally they are carrying (see [[carry_downed]]).
- Recruits following your side within 2 tiles.
- A vehicle's load, if someone drives it home.

## The end of a run

The run ends once everyone has extracted, died or been left behind. Party members who never got out are dead, and their gear is lost.

## Leaving for now

Leaving the screen is not extracting: the party stays in the zone and you can resume later from the expedition menu.

## Tips

- Extract the heavily loaded first; they are slow and loud.
- With an ally still up, a downed survivor is not lost yet.

topics.title: Downed allies
topics.short: A survivor at 0 HP is downed and bleeds out in a few rounds. Revive them with a med-kit or blood bag, or carry them out (C).
topics.long:
A survivor brought to 0 HP is **downed**: they cannot act and will bleed out after about 3 rounds. A very heavy hit kills outright.

## Saving them

- **Revive** from an adjacent tile (2 AP): a med-kit gets them up with 15 HP, a field trauma kit with 30, a blood bag with 45. Items work on any survivor who is not hostile, allies included.
- The Triage perk adds HP on revival and extra rounds before bleeding out.

## Carrying

- **C** next to a downed ally lifts them for 1 AP. They ride on your tile.
- You move one tile less and lose special moves (such as a jump).
- Put them down for free; if you go down, you drop them.
- When you extract, they come with you and go home to their own colony.

## Tips

- A downed survivor is still in play while an ally is up.
- Revive before moving if you can: carrying makes you slow and easy to catch.

topics.title: Co-op
topics.short: Allies share one side: one fog of war, no friendly fire, and watching each other's backs. Loot and survivors stay with their own player.
topics.long:
In a co-op mission, or once an alliance forms, allied parties are one **team**.

## Shared

- Sight: what any ally sees, every contact, sensor and explored tile is the team's.
- No friendly fire; overwatch never fires on allies.
- An ally next to you halves an ambush against you (see [[ambush]]).

## Kept apart

- Turns, ownership, loot and results stay per player. Loot is first come, first served.
- Hand an item to an adjacent ally with **Give** (1 AP); it goes home with them.
- Heal or revive an ally with your own items, or carry them out (see [[carry_downed]]).
- A recruit joins whoever escorts it out.

## Difficulty

There are more enemies for each extra player in the mission.

## Talking

Mark tiles for your team with [[pings]].

## Tips

- Trade with your ally afterwards, live, between missions (see [[trading]]).

topics.title: Alliances
topics.short: Meet another party in the field and offer an alliance. If they accept, you share sight. Breaking one gives everyone a round's warning.
topics.long:
In a versus mission you may run into another player's party.

## Offering

- When your party and theirs see each other, offer an alliance on your turn (free).
- They answer on their own turn. The offer lapses after 2 rounds.
- On accept, both parties join one team at once and share sight (see [[coop]]).

## Breaking

- Announce the break on your turn. It takes effect after a full round's warning, with a banner for everyone, so there is no instant backstab.
- Each side keeps a copy of what the team knew. Motion sensors and pings go with whoever placed them; carried allies are put down.
- From then on, sight is separate and fire is open.

## Tips

- An alliance halves ambushes against people standing next to each other and doubles your eyes; it costs nothing until it breaks.
- Watch the break banner: when it shows, step away from your former allies.

topics.title: Pings
topics.short: Mark a tile for your team: danger, go here or loot. Two per turn, free, gone after two rounds.
topics.long:
A **ping** puts a marker on a tile that only your team sees.

## Kinds

- **Danger**: something is there.
- **Go here**: a place to move to.
- **Loot**: something worth picking up.

## Limits

- Free: it costs no AP.
- Up to 2 per turn; more with radios.
- Each fades after 2 rounds.

## Tips

- Ping a contact you heard but cannot see, so your ally knows where to point their lookout.
- Pings are private to your team, so they never give your position away.

topics.title: Tactical cards
topics.short: Your squad shares a hand of cards. Most cost card points, not AP; points refill each round.
topics.long:
## The hand

- One shared deck per party. Each round the hand refills to its size and the card points refill to the budget.
- Played cards go to the used pile and come back when the draw pile runs out; consumable cards are gone for good.

## Playing a card

- Pick a card, then pick who it goes on. The picker shows who can take it now and, for the rest, why not.
- **Hard** cards need a qualified character (a skill, attribute or perk). **Baseline** cards work for anyone; a qualified character gets more.
- Some cost AP; some take extra AP for a **boost**. Arm-heavy cards wait for working arms.
- **Reactions** answer a seen enemy's telegraphed plan, also on another unit's turn.
- A hard card nobody can use can be discarded for free, once a round.

## Slots

Some characters hold personal slot cards: always to hand for them, paid from the squad's points.

topics.title: Telegraphs and threats
topics.short: Enemies show what they will do next turn: the path they walk and the tile they strike. Step off it.
topics.long:
## Telegraphs

- An enemy that has to move to reach you declares its plan: a trail of steps and a ring on the tile it will strike. It carries it out at the start of its next turn.
- An enemy already in reach strikes at once. Turrets always telegraph their aim.
- A blow on an empty tile hits nothing. Dodge one and your next attack on that enemy gets +20% to hit.

## The threat overlay

- Strong red: a telegraphed blow lands here.
- Faint orange: a seen enemy could hit this tile from where it stands.

## Hit preview

Hover a hostile with an attack chosen: every tile you can move to shows your hit chance from there.

topics.title: The bestiary
topics.short: What your colony knows of each enemy type grows with every sighting, fight and kill.
topics.long:
- **Seen**: its weapons and reach.
- **Fought**: its AP and how it moves.
- **Killed**: everything: health, armor, stats and how it behaves.

What a party learns comes home only if someone gets out. Other players are never in it: judge them by their gear and play.
